why: Found at the build's first run of holon rank, before P1's upper bound was compared: layout_bound required each encoder's own argument to carry a version premise, so for the three cross-component codec laws, whose Go side's binder (BatchHeaderV0 or BatchHeaderV1) has no version field, it returned None and P1's test could compare no upper bound. The contract's M-PAR takes 'the claim's two encoder layouts, at the versions its premises pin'; each of these laws pins one version (k.version), and the codec document keys each Go encoder's one layout by that version, which is how holon.rules.par derives the laws (_cross_linked pairs both sides with _layout_linked(doc, fn, v) at the law's v). The amended function takes a side's own version premise, else the one version the premises pin; nothing else changed. holon/measures.py had the same misreading and was fixed the same way in the build. The corrected bound was computed only after this amendment was committed; the buggy run showed only that no upper bound was computed (the lower bound, 32 positions, is the records' difference, read before the prereg).

Found at the build's first run of holon rank: replay/M3/sorts/report.json records each witness run's model observations as outcome strings ('ok', 'rev panic:0x11'; holon.sorts.run3), not observation objects, so rule K5's reader called .get on a string and raised. The contract's K5 (a witness run that ends in a revert on the model) is unchanged; the amended reader takes an outcome string that starts with 'rev' (or an object whose status is revert) as a revert. holon/rank.py read it the same way and was fixed the same way; its corrected run gives the SORT realize law revert and the SORT tag law store, as I81-P3 predicts.

I71 (tests_m3/test_undo_cancel.py rules C7-C8, merged after I81's prereg) adds UNDO's cancel sub-form. A cancel law's run without x keeps y (prefix, y, t), so its replay entry (holon.undo.run.replay_entry) carries t_at_without, the first index of t in that run. The instrument read every UNDO entry as a pair's, with t at t_at - 2 in the run without the pair, so for the cancel law it compared t[0] with y's own step. It found a divergence at t[0] whatever the continuation, and gave channel 'store' where the runs' first divergent step, claimReward, is ok in one run and reverts in the other ('revert'). R7 then failed on the cancel law alone. Amended to read t_at_without where the entry carries it. Pair and residue entries carry none and read exactly as before, so every value the instrument computes for I81's own laws is unchanged. holon.measures and holon.rank have the same fix (I71's 019101d).

I90 (tests_m3/test_go_counts.py rules C3, C5 and C8, preregistered with I90 in spec/M3/predictions.json) adds one REFUTED PAR law over a Go count document, gen/M3/goops/l1_counts.json, whose witness's two sides are counts (65536 against 0): holon.measures.par gives it a value defect, kind value 1, certified, as for every scalar difference. I81-P1's last assertion counted the measure kinds of every REFUTED PAR record of results/M3, {bytes: 3, value: 5}, which is a claim about the base's laws (I81 predicts over the M3 laws that exist today). The amended test counts over base_law_ids() only, as I81-P5 already does; every per-law assertion, the count law's included, is unchanged.

I84: I84's build (holon-rules/1.10, BUILD_PLAN row I84) adds PAR laws of sub-form link_domain over I80's bundle declaration; two are REFUTED (results/M3/L_par_ldom_Rollup_commitBatchWithProof_*.json and ..._proveCommittedBatchState_*), and holon rank measures them over values (kind value, 1 bit, certified), so the test's count of REFUTED PAR laws by defect kind became {bytes 3, value 7} against I81's {bytes 3, value 5}. The amended loop leaves out the link_domain laws; every assertion on I81's PAR laws, and the per-law checks the two new records also pass, are unchanged.

I44 (= I44b; spec/M3/predictions/I44.json, amended at its prereg) computes NAT's naturality defect mass over I29's NAT laws, which merged after I81's prereg (I29, 918b9a4e: 9 NAT laws in laws/M3). I81's contract M-NAT reads 'pending (I29) for any NAT law; rules.NAT is pending I29 when no NAT law exists', written when no NAT law existed, and test_p5 asserted rules.NAT pending I29 unconditionally. I44's M-NAT (the docstring of tests_m3/test_measures_i44.py) replaces I81's, and the sidecar spec/M3/lib/ranking.json, amended at I44's prereg, names no NAT pending key, so rules.NAT is computed. Amended: rules.NAT must be pending I29 while laws/M3 holds no NAT law, exactly as before, and computed with no pending key once one exists. The kinds over the base's 136 laws (which hold no NAT law) and the one-measure-per-law check are unchanged. No other I81 claim, prediction, regression or documented miss moves.
